rule_text: A change gets at most three review rounds. Decision `hold-unsafe-after-round-3` (net-value hold after round 3) holds the delete-only change's one round, the held change that is also red, and the merge at zero or positive net value. Rounds 1 and 2 still fix the defect (`outcomes-tests-are-statements`). After round 3, a change that changes a guard or check (`hold-unsafe-after-round-3`, net-value hold after round 3) gets the net-value test. The round-3 reviewer judges its net safety value against main: safety holes closed against safety holes opened, weighted by expected harm. A change that changes no guard or check skips the test and merges on green. A safety hole is a guard or check that lets through an act that main refuses or asks about. Turning a main refusal into an ask is also a safety hole. For any guard or check, an act counts only if Claude could write it by mistake or from a misread task. A form only an attacker would write does not count (`guard-guards-mistakes-only`, guards stop Claude's mistakes, not an attacker). An act that my typed override lets through is not a safety hole (`owner-override`, my typed override). For every change, each open finding becomes a debt or a note, pointing to its decision (`roles-findings-are-debts-or-notes`). A change with negative net value is held: remove it from the batch, so the rest merges green. A held change is parked. It gets no fix lane and no more work until the owner decides. After round 3, red CI is not a named safety hole: split it, ship the passing part, and open the red part as a new lane. That lane starts at round 1, try 1. Its brief records what failed; if no split works or the test looks stale, ask the owner (`outcomes-stale-decision-protocol`); never weaken a test to reach green. A red batch still drops the lane first (`git-integration-branch-merge`); the split happens in that lane's own fix. A small fix to a round's finding gets a fix check and merges on green. A FAIL or a wider diff starts a new lane at round 1.
